title: Calibrate windowed aggregation and explainability for model cost charts
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Symptom: Console per-model cost charts and per-route attribution are showing transient negative deltas and non-monotonic spikes after nightly backfills and rate-limit retry storms. Root cause hypothesis: multiple independent issues amplify each other — (1) aggregation windows for streaming and batch ingestion use different boundary semantics (event_time vs ingest_time) which leads to double-counts and retractions when late events are backfilled; (2) rate-limited requests that are retried produce duplicate telemetry with inconsistent request_ids and tokenization metadata, making idempotency by request_id unreliable; (3) quota tiling logic (sharded per-customer buckets) applies rounding and per-shard compensation that can move small fractional token attributions across different model buckets on reconciliation. Impact: dashboards show incorrect hourly breakdowns, customers see temporary under/over charges in the console, automated alerts fire for quota breaches that are not customer-visible. This ticket will (a) define canonical aggregation rules for console charts (prefer event_time with a configurable lateness window and clear retraction policy), (b) implement an explainability layer that surfaces how much of a chart bar is from backfilled vs realtime ingest, (c) make backfill processors idempotent by event_id + canonicalized token_counts, (d) change quota tiling to use monotonic counters and a single deterministic tie-breaker for fractional attributions, and (e) ship a safe reconciliation job to correct existing materialized aggregates and surface a remediation report in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Console hourly and daily per-model charts remain monotonic across backfills: retrospective re-attributions only adjust historical bars and do not produce negative deltas for a single bucket
New explainability toggle in Console shows percent of tokens from backfill vs realtime for each bar
Backfill ingestion job is idempotent by event_id and rejects conflicting duplicates in the same logical window
Quota tiling uses monotonic counters with deterministic shard assignment and produces stable fractional attributions after reconciliation
Reconciliation job runs without increasing latency on user-facing queries and produces a remediation CSV for billing review
technical_notes: Planned approach: 1) Add an ingestion shim that normalizes timestamps: set canonical_event_ts = event.event_time || fallback event.ingest_time and attach lateness_ms. 2) Change windowing to use event_time fixed windows with allowed_lateness = 15m (configurable per-customer). 3) Implement upsert semantics in the aggregate store keyed by event_id (etags for token_count) to make backfills idempotent. 4) Replace shard compensation heuristics with monotonic counters stored in per-customer ledger and deterministic rounding (round-to-nearest with consistent tie-breaker). 5) Add explainability fields to aggregate rows: source=[realtime|backfill], original_ingest_ts, reconciled_by. 6) Provide a lightweight reconciliation job (non-blocking) that computes diffs and writes remediation artifacts to GCS for billing ops review. Consider performance impact: must avoid cross-shard read amplification; implement reconciliation with map-reduce over shards and sample-first passes to bound runtime.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reconciliation runtime could be long and impact warehouse I/O. Mitigation: run initial pass as sampled delta and then full pass in off-peak with throttling.

Risk: Changing window semantics could change visible historical charts and confuse customers. Mitigation: expose explainability toggle and a changelog entry, and coordinate with billing ops for rollforward communication.
Risk: Idempotency keys may not exist for older events. Mitigation: fall back to (request_hash + ingest_ts) heuristic and mark those rows as best-effort in reconciliation report.

Risk: Deterministic tie-breaker rounding may shift fractional attributions across models. Mitigation: include a correction step in reconciliation and surface corrected amounts in a remediation CSV for accounting review.
